chapter: Owls, Werlein's and the OK record
title: The Owls and other New Orleans orchestras
summary: Brownlee names members of the Owls, another good New Orleans orchestra, and notes there were many good bands.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Well, it was quite a nice home. We played up there many times with my orchestra after theater parties and things like that. He called me as late as 8.30 in the evening, maybe 9 o'clock, asked me if I could get the boys together and come up. We'd do it. We'd get together and go on up and play a job for them. Have a lot of fun at the same time. Did I mention anything about the Owls being on our taping here? Very little.
Very little. Just sort of in-
Monk Smith and Benji White and- I see.

And Young Mackie, Red's brother. Dick. Dick. Dick Mackie. That's right. And what was Earl's last name? Earl Crumb. Earl Crumb, yes. Earl Crumb. Oh, yeah. Well, that was a fine outfit. They used to have a nice band.
There were several outstanding orchestras around besides you, is there?
